title: Remediate: unbounded recursion compiling nested choice blocks (compiler/directives.py)
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review]
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/compiler/directives.py

**Finding**:
`compile_choice` -> `_compile_directive_bodies` -> `compile_directive` -> `compile_choice` form mutual recursion with no depth limit when compiling nested `choice:` blocks in a `.ravel` story file. A story file with deeply nested choices (verified reproducible at depth ~3000 using the actual compiler functions) crashes the compiler with an unhandled `RecursionError` instead of a typed `ParseError`, and on some interpreters/thread stack sizes this class of unbounded recursion can exhaust the C stack outright. Story files are an untrusted-input surface for this engine (shared/downloaded stories, or story content an attacker can influence).

**Fix suggestion**:
Add an explicit depth counter/parameter threaded through `compile_directives`/`_compile_directive_bodies`/`compile_directive`/`compile_choice`, and raise `ravel.exceptions.ParseError` (not `RecursionError`) once a configured `MAX_CHOICE_NESTING_DEPTH` is exceeded. Add a regression test compiling a synthetically deep nested-choice story and asserting a `ParseError`, not a crash.

**Acceptance**:
- Compiling a story with nested `choice:` blocks beyond the configured limit raises `ParseError` (never `RecursionError`)
- A test exercises the limit at both the boundary and one level past it
- Normal, reasonably-nested stories (e.g. examples/cloak) still compile unchanged
close_reason: Added MAX_CHOICE_NESTING_DEPTH guard so deep choice nesting raises ParseError, not RecursionError

title: Remediate: path traversal in FileSystemLoader.get_source via untrusted include: names
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review]
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/loaders.py, src/ravel/adapters/story_source.py

**Finding**:
`FileSystemLoader.get_source` (src/ravel/loaders.py) builds `filepath = Path(self.base_path) / (name + self.extension)` where `name` comes straight from an `include:` entry in a compiled `.ravel` rulebook (src/ravel/compiler/rulebooks.py: `includes.extend(get_list_of_texts(rule[1]))`), with no sanitization. `pathlib` joins an absolute-looking segment by discarding the base entirely, and `../` segments are followed normally, so a story author can write `include: ["../../../../some/other/dir/name"]` (or an absolute path) to make the loader read a file outside `base_path`, as long as a file at that resolved path plus the `.ravel` extension exists. This is now directly reachable from the new Clean-Architecture entry point, `FileSystemStorySource.load()` -> `Environment(loader=FileSystemLoader(...))`, which is the path production code uses to compile untrusted story directories.

**Fix suggestion**:
In `FileSystemLoader.get_source`, resolve `filepath` and reject (raise `ravel.exceptions.RulebookNotFound` or a new typed error) any resolved path that is not a descendant of the resolved `base_path` (e.g. compare via `Path.resolve()` + `relative_to()`/`os.path.commonpath`, not string prefix matching). Also consider rejecting `name` values containing path separators or leading `/` at the point `include:` names are collected, since a rule name is not supposed to encode a filesystem path.

**Acceptance**:
- An `include:` value that attempts to escape `base_path` (via `../` or an absolute path) fails to load instead of reading the out-of-tree file
- A regression test constructs a story tree plus a sibling file outside it and asserts the escape attempt is refused
- Existing legitimate same-directory / subdirectory includes still resolve correctly
close_reason: Reject include names that escape base_path via ../, absolute paths, or symlinks in FileSystemLoader.get_source

title: Remediate: string repetition and % formatting allow unbounded memory allocation
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review]
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/types.py

**Finding**:
Expression (types.py:101-117) and Operation (types.py:139-160) apply op.mul/op.mod to any operands, so `x = "a" * 100000000000`, `x = "%999999999d" % 1`, or `x *= 2` on a string quality allocate unbounded memory (verified "ab" * 3 and "%5d" % 7 evaluate). In Expression.evaluate and Operation.evaluate, reject str operands for every arithmetic operator except + (and =) by raising EvaluationError before calling the operator. Document the rule in docs/RAVEL_LANGUAGE_SPEC.md and specs/002-spec-compliance/contracts/evaluation.md.

title: Remediate: oversized integer literals escape as untyped VisitationError
description:

**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/grammars.py, src/ravel/parsers.py

**Finding**:
The integer terminal (grammars.py:60, now `-?\\d+`) accepts unbounded digit runs; visit_integer calls int() and a 5000-digit literal hits Python's int_max_str_digits limit, surfacing as parsimonious VisitationError(ValueError) instead of a typed ravel ParseError (verified for both operations and comparisons).

**Fix suggestion**:
Add ValueError handling in visit_integer/visit_float (or a digit-count cap in the grammar) that raises OperationParseError/ParseError naming the literal; ensure the parse wrappers unwrap it.

title: Remediate: string qualities grow without bound through + concatenation
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review] (harden cycle 2)
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/engine/state.py:29, src/ravel/types.py (Expression.evaluate / Operation.evaluate)

**Finding**:
_is_storable bounds ints (INT_QUALITY_RANGE) and floats (isfinite) but not strings. ravel-h6v.10 only blocked non-+ string arithmetic, so s += s doubles per line and s = s + s + ... (100 operands) multiplies by 100 per line. Measured: 22 given lines of 's += s' -> 8 MB; 4 lines of a 100-operand chain (1.6 KB of source) -> 200 MB string, 400 MB peak at engine.start with no player input. About 35 doubling lines, or 5 chain lines, exhausts memory.

**Fix suggestion**:
- Add MAX_STRING_QUALITY_LENGTH (e.g. 64 KiB) next to INT_QUALITY_RANGE and enforce it in _is_storable, so Qualities.set rejects oversize strings with InvalidQualityValueError.
- In Expression.evaluate and Operation.evaluate, check len(left) + len(right) against the same cap before concatenating strings and raise EvaluationError, so a single 100-operand chain cannot allocate the oversize intermediate first.

**Acceptance**:
- given 's = "ab"' plus 30 lines of 's += s' raises InvalidOperationError/InvalidQualityValueError, with peak memory well under 10 MB
- a 100-operand 's + s + ...' chain whose result would exceed the cap raises a typed error before allocation
- string concatenation under the cap still works; 100% coverage holds
close_reason: Cap string + at 64 KiB before concatenating; storage guard; Limits appendix in spec

title: Remediate: expression parsing amplifies long lines before any size gate
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review] (harden cycle 2)
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/parsers.py:43 (BaseExpressionParser.parse), src/ravel/parsers.py:90 (_fold_left)

**Finding**:
The ravel-h6v.8/.9 operand and depth caps run in the visitor after Parsimonious has built the full packrat parse tree, so they bound evaluator recursion but not parser memory or CPU. Measured: a 200 KB 'y = x+x+...' line takes 7.8 s and 412 MB peak before the operand cap rejects it (about 2000x amplification, linear). A 131 KB nested-parens expression within the caps compiles in 4.4 s at 184 MB, then its 64k-operand int64 product takes 2 s to evaluate. Not ReDoS; pure linear blowup with no upper bound on expression text.

**Fix suggestion**:
- Add MAX_EXPRESSION_LENGTH (e.g. 2048 chars) and check len(text) in the existing BaseExpressionParser.parse pre-scan, raising operand_limit_error before super().parse.
- Scope it to expression parsers only: PlainTextParser/IntroTextParser subclass ComparisonParser, and long prose lines are legitimate and cheap (200 KB prose parses in 0.02 s). Exempt them via a class attribute (max_length = None) or gate only the {...} prefix.

**Acceptance**:
- a 200 KB operation or comparison raises OperationParseError/ComparisonParseError in under 50 ms with no large allocation
- a 200 KB plain-text line still compiles
- existing .8/.9/.11 tests stay green
close_reason: Gate expression text at 64 KiB before parsing (expressions only); spec Limits row + tests

comments.author: eykd
comments.text: Orchestrator note: gate expression text length BEFORE parsimonious parses it (expressions only; long plain-text lines are legitimate). Add the cap to the language spec's Limits section (added by ravel-h6v.12).

title: Remediate: deeply nested rulebook blocks raise untyped RecursionError from Environment.load
description:

**Finding**:
syml.parsers.parse(...).as_source() recurses once per indentation level. A rulebook with about 300 nested choice blocks (a few KB of text) makes Environment.load() raise a raw RecursionError from syml/nodes.py instead of a typed ravel.exceptions error. - Optionally pre-scan leading-whitespace depth and reject past a MAX_NESTING constant before calling syml.

**Acceptance**:

- examples/cloak still loads

title: Remediate: FileSystemLoader reads rulebooks without a size bound or typed read errors
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review] (harden cycle 2)
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/loaders.py:48 (FileSystemLoader.get_source)

**Finding**:
get_source calls fi.read() with no size limit, so a huge .ravel file (or an include of one) is read fully into memory and then fed to the parsers, which amplify it (see the expression parsing amplification task). It also leaks raw exceptions on bad input: non-UTF-8 bytes raise UnicodeDecodeError, a directory named x.ravel raises IsADirectoryError, and a name containing NUL raises ValueError, where callers expect RulebookNotFound or ParseError. The path-traversal guard (resolve + is_relative_to) holds.

**Fix suggestion**:
- Add MAX_RULEBOOK_BYTES (e.g. 1 MiB): read limit+1 bytes in binary mode, and raise a typed error if exceeded (same pattern as FileSaveStore.read with MAX_SAVE_BYTES).
- Decode UTF-8 explicitly and map UnicodeDecodeError to exceptions.ParseError naming the rulebook (relative name only, no absolute path).
- Require filepath.is_file() and treat ValueError/IsADirectoryError as RulebookNotFound.

**Acceptance**:
- an oversize .ravel file raises a typed error without reading more than the limit+1 bytes
- non-UTF-8 file, directory-named rulebook, and NUL-containing name each raise a ravel.exceptions type
- error messages do not include the absolute base path
close_reason: Cap rulebook source at 1 MiB in both loaders; typed errors for decode/dir/NUL; spec Limits row

comments.text: Orchestrator note: cap rulebook source bytes in the loaders and map UnicodeDecodeError / IsADirectoryError / NUL-name ValueError to typed ravel errors. Add the source-size cap to the language spec's Limits section (added by ravel-h6v.12).

title: Remediate: unstorable-value error formatting raises raw ValueError on huge computed ints
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review] (harden cycle 2)
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/engine/state.py:45 (_validate_quality)

**Finding**:
_validate_quality builds its message with %r of the rejected value. When an expression computes an int past 4300 digits (two 4000-digit literals multiplied, or a wide nested product of int64 qualities), repr() raises ValueError (int max str digits) before InvalidQualityValueError exists, so engine.start/choose leak an untyped ValueError. The same formatting would also embed a multi-hundred-MB string for an oversize string quality. Computed-value sibling of ravel-h6v.11 (oversize literal).

**Fix suggestion**:
- Format the rejected value safely: for int, report type and bit_length(); for str, report length plus a truncated preview (e.g. first 40 chars); never repr the full value.
- Apply the same bounded formatting anywhere EvaluationError/InvalidOperationError interpolates operand values.

**Acceptance**:
- 'y = <4000-digit literal> * <4000-digit literal>' raises InvalidQualityValueError (or InvalidOperationError), not ValueError
- the error message is under 200 characters regardless of value size
close_reason: Bounded unstorable-value message (bit length / truncated preview); computed oversize int now raises typed error

title: Remediate: plain-text {...} predicate prefix bypasses the expression length gate
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review]
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/parsers.py, docs/RAVEL_LANGUAGE_SPEC.md

**Finding**:
PlainTextParser sets max_length = None (parsers.py:171), exempting the whole text line from MAX_EXPRESSION_LENGTH. But a text line's `{quality == expr}` prefix is an expression parsed by the same comparison grammar, so it bypasses the 64 KiB pre-parse gate that ravel-h6v.13 added. Measured: a single in-bounds 1 MiB rulebook line `{q == 1 + 1 + ...} hello` costs 47.5 s and ~995 MB peak before the operand-cap ComparisonParseError; a 240 KB line costs 5 s / 234 MB. The unclosed variant (`{q == 1 + 1 + ...` with no `}`) costs the same (81 MB per 80 KB) and is then silently accepted as prose.

**Fix suggestion**:
Override PlainTextParser.parse: when the line starts with `{`, measure the brace span (text[1:text.find("}")], or the rest of the line when there is no `}`) and raise ComparisonParseError if it exceeds MAX_EXPRESSION_LENGTH before calling the grammar. Keep prose after the prefix exempt. Reword the spec §E Limits row to "prose is exempt; the `{…}` prefix of a text line is not".

**Acceptance**:
- A text line whose `{...}` prefix exceeds 65,536 characters raises ComparisonParseError (a ParseError) before Parsimonious runs (test: under ~0.1 s for a 1 MiB line)
- Same for an unclosed `{` prefix longer than the cap
- Long plain prose lines without a `{` prefix still compile
- docs/RAVEL_LANGUAGE_SPEC.md §E row updated
close_reason: Gate text-line {...} prefix length pre-parse; spec E row reworded; tests added

comments.author: eykd
comments.text: DAVID RULING 2026-09-28: in scope as a bypass of a declared cap. Check the {…} prefix length against MAX_EXPRESSION_LENGTH before parsimonious runs (including the unclosed-brace case, which must not pay parse cost before being treated as prose). Reword the §E Limits row so it is accurate.

title: Remediate: common when predicates are recompiled per rule giving quadratic load cost
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review]
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/compiler/rulebooks.py, src/ravel/compiler/rulesets.py

**Finding**:
compile_rulebook passes `preamble["common_predicates"] + ruleset_predicates` to compile_ruleset for every rule (rulebooks.py:121), so a file's K top-level `when:` predicates are re-parsed by Parsimonious and re-sorted once per rule: cost is K x M. Measured: K=M=400 from a 10 KB source takes 9.6 s / 31 MB (K=M=200: 2.4 s). A 1 MiB rulebook, within every §E cap, can hold tens of thousands of each, so Environment.load runs for hours or days. Query-time cost per turn also scales with K x M predicate checks.

**Fix suggestion**:
Compile common_predicates once per file (in compile_preamble or before the rule loop) and reuse those Predicate objects. Share one pre-sorted tuple by reference instead of re-sorting and copying K entries into every rule. Because query-time evaluation still costs K x M per turn, also cap the total compiled predicate references per story (for example 100,000), raising a typed ParseError and documenting it in docs/RAVEL_LANGUAGE_SPEC.md §E Limits.

**Acceptance**:
- Each common predicate is parsed exactly once per file (test via a counting spy on ComparisonParser.parse)
- K=M=2000 loads in under a few seconds with bounded peak memory (assert both time and tracemalloc peak)
- A story exceeding the new total-predicate cap raises a ParseError; the cap is documented in §E
- Rule ordering and specificity scoring are unchanged (existing query tests pass)
close_reason: Compile common when: predicates once per file, shared across rules; VM spec compute note; PD-19 recorded

comments.author: eykd
comments.text: DAVID RULING 2026-09-28 (threat model): caps bound INPUT SIZE, not total compute. Fix .18 by compiling a file's common when: predicates ONCE per file and sharing one pre-sorted tuple across its rules. Do NOT add a new cap on total predicate references. Also in this task: (1) add a short paragraph to docs/RAVEL_VM_SPEC.md (next to the save-integrity-is-the-host's-job note) stating that the Limits caps bound input size, not total compile or per-turn compute, so hosts running untrusted stories must wrap load and each engine call in their own timeout/sandbox; (2) record the ruling as a dated decision in specs/002-spec-compliance/research.md.

title: Remediate: syml syntax errors escape the ravel ParseError hierarchy
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review]
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/environments.py

**Finding**:
Environment.compile_rulebook wraps syml.parsers.parse only for RecursionError (environments.py:103-106). Malformed rulebook syntax raises syml.exceptions.DuplicateKeyError, TabIndentationError or OutOfContextNodeError, all subclasses of syml's own ParseError(ValueError), not ravel.exceptions.ParseError. A host that catches ravel's ParseError, as §E and the spec promise for rejected input, lets these escape. Verified with "r:\n\t- hi\n" (TabIndentationError) and a duplicate top-level rule key.

**Fix suggestion**:
Add `except syml.exceptions.ParseError as error: raise exceptions.ParseError(str(error)) from error`. str(error) is already bounded by syml's windowing. Keep the RecursionError clause.

**Acceptance**:
- Tab indentation, a duplicate key and an out-of-context node each raise ravel.exceptions.ParseError, with the syml error chained as __cause__
- The message keeps the filename:line:column prefix

title: Remediate: parse error messages echo unbounded rulebook source text
description:

Include names reach RulebookNotFound("%s: ...") unescaped, so control characters or ANSI escapes in a hostile include name flow into terminals and logs. Add one helper that renders source excerpts through a bounded, printable window (for example 80 code points with an ellipsis, escaping non-printables the way syml's _truncated_window/_printable do). Use it in raise_parse_error, the directive-compiler messages, get_text's error and the loader's name interpolation. Keep the full Source on the exception's args or attributes for programmatic use.

title: Remediate: brackets or unquoted names end the predicate prefix scan early, bypassing the length cap
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review] (harden cycle 4)
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/parsers.py:180-190 (PlainTextParser._prefix_span / parse)

**Finding**:
This is a hole left by the ravel-h6v.17 fix. The gate regex ends the {...} prefix at the first } outside a quoted string. But the grammar also lets } appear inside a [bracketed] quality (bracketed_quality = [^\]]+) and inside an unquoted simple_quality ([^\s]+). So the regex measures a short prefix while the grammar keeps parsing. A 200,000-char predicate then compiles, beating the 65,536-char cap in docs/RAVEL_LANGUAGE_SPEC.md §E. Verified:
  '{x == [a}] + "' + 'a'*200000 + '"} hi'   -> parsed
  '{[q}] == "' + 'a'*200000 + '"} hi'        -> parsed
  '{q}} == "' + 'a'*200000 + '"} hi'         -> parsed
(control: '{x == "<200K>"} hi' is correctly refused with ComparisonParseError)

**Fix suggestion**:
The regex must never stop earlier than the grammar would. Pick one:
(a) Fail safe: over-approximate the span, for example measure up to the LAST } on the line, or the whole line when it starts with {. The only side effect is refusing a >65K prose line that contains a late brace.
(b) Match the grammar: consume \[[^\]]*\] as one unit in the regex, and stop simple_quality from matching }. Option (b) changes the language, so check what RAVEL_LANGUAGE_SPEC.md says about unquoted quality-name characters first.

**Acceptance**:
- All three probe lines above raise ComparisonParseError with the length message.
- '{x == "a}b"} prose' and '{x == 1} prose with a } brace' still parse as before.
- A regression test for each bypass shape sits alongside the ravel-h6v.17 tests; 100% branch coverage holds.
close_reason: Prefix matched in bounded MAX+2 window; bypass regressions + property test added

title: Remediate: malformed rulebook shapes raise raw AttributeError TypeError KeyError from Environment.load
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review] (harden cycle 4)
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/compiler/rulebooks.py:46 (compile_about), :56 (compile_preamble), :101 (compile_rulebook); src/ravel/environments.py:113

**Finding**:
When a rulebook has the wrong structure, Environment.load / MemoryStorySource.load / FileSystemStorySource.load raise raw Python exceptions instead of ravel.exceptions.*. That breaks the story_source.py docstring contract ('raises ravel.exceptions.* on bad source'). Verified inputs:
  '' or '# c' or 'hello' or '- a'        -> AttributeError (rulebooks.py:56, top level is not a mapping)
  'foo: bar' or 'foo:'                    -> TypeError 'Source' object is not subscriptable (:101)
  'foo:\n    a: b' or 'foo:\n    a: a: hi'  -> KeyError: 0 (:101, rule body is a mapping)
  'about:\n    - a' or 'about: x'          -> AttributeError (:46, about is not a mapping)
  line containing U+2028 inside a list item -> TypeError (:101)

**Fix suggestion**:
Add shape checks that raise ParseError naming the rule. The rulebook must be a Mapping, each rule's data a non-empty Sequence, and about a Mapping. As a backstop, wrap rulebooks.compile_rulebook in Environment.compile_rulebook the way app/saves.decode_save does. Caution: MissingBaggageError and RulebookNotFound are not ParseError subclasses, so any blanket wrap must re-raise ravel exception types unchanged before converting (AttributeError, TypeError, KeyError, IndexError) into ParseError. Bound the rule excerpt in the message with exceptions.bounded_repr.

**Acceptance**:
- Each input above raises a ravel.exceptions.ParseError subclass from MemoryStorySource.load.
- MissingBaggageError and RulebookNotFound keep their existing types (existing tests stay green).
- A parametrized test covers each shape; 100% branch coverage holds.
close_reason: Shape checks in rulebooks.py raise ParseError; tests via MemoryStorySource

title: Remediate: unclosed bracket in intro text raises raw parsimonious IncompleteParseError
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review] (harden cycle 4)
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/parsers.py:145 (IntroTextParser); call sites src/ravel/compiler/directives.py:22 (compile_directives) and :92 (compile_choice)

**Finding**:
When a situation's first line or a choice label has an unmatched '[' (for example 'foo:\n    - [unclosed', 'choice: [x', or an ANSI escape such as \x1b[2J), parsimonious raises IncompleteParseError. That class is not a ravel ParseError, so it escapes Environment.load untyped. Ordinary authors can trigger it with prose like 'Price: 5 [approx'.

**Fix suggestion**:
Give IntroTextParser a parse() override that catches exceptions.ParsimoniousParseError and re-raises exceptions.ParseError with a bounded_repr excerpt, the same pattern OperationParser.parse uses. Or relax the grammar so that a lone '[' is plain head text (this changes behavior; check RAVEL_LANGUAGE_SPEC.md on [bracketed] intro text first).

**Acceptance**:
- 'foo:\n    - [unclosed' and a choice label '[x' both raise a ravel.exceptions.ParseError subclass (or compile as plain text, if the grammar route is chosen and documented).
- Tests cover both call sites; 100% branch coverage holds.
close_reason: Wrap IntroTextParser ParseError as typed ravel ParseError with bounded excerpt

title: Remediate: save decode errors echo unbounded save-supplied keys names and locations
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review] (harden cycle 4)
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/app/saves.py:68, :144, :181-189, :255

**Finding**:
SaveCorruptError and UnsupportedSaveVersionError messages embed save-file values with a bare %r: duplicate keys, quality names, frame locations, and format_version. A hostile save can therefore put up to about 1 MiB of its own text into the error that CLI prints as 'Could not load: ...' and that hosts log. The 1 MiB save cap bounds it, but it is still inconsistent with the ravel-h6v.20 fix, which bounded source excerpts in parse errors.

**Fix suggestion**:
Pass these values through a bounded, printable excerpt helper (the same logic as exceptions.bounded_repr). Check Constitution VII layering before importing ravel.exceptions into ravel.app, since that module imports parsimonious and syml. If the import is not allowed, move printable/bounded_repr to ravel.utils.strings and re-export them from ravel.exceptions.

**Acceptance**:
- A save with a 500 KB duplicate key, quality name, or stack location raises SaveCorruptError whose str() is under ~200 characters.
- Control characters in those values come out escaped.
- Existing save tests stay green; 100% branch coverage holds.
close_reason: Save decode errors use bounded printable excerpts via ravel.utils.excerpts

title: Remediate: console adapter echoes story control characters and terminal escapes unfiltered
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review] (harden cycle 4)
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/cli.py:107-120 (ConsoleUI._render_one)

**Finding**:
Story text, choice labels, quality names/values, and locations go straight to click.echo. A .ravel file can carry raw control characters. Verified: '"\x1b]0;pwned\x07hello"' compiles to Text(text='"\x1b]0;pwned\x07hello"'), and that reaches TextShown unchanged. Running an untrusted story with 'ravel run' lets it send terminal escape sequences: retitling the window, clearing the screen, and on some terminals writing the clipboard (OSC 52). Error messages were already escaped for this reason (exceptions.printable); game output was not.

**Fix suggestion**:
In ConsoleUI, send every rendered string through a sanitizer that escapes non-printable characters except newline (and optionally tab). Reuse the printable() escaping logic without truncation. Leave the engine outputs unchanged; this is the adapter's job.

**Acceptance**:

- Normal text, including non-ASCII printable text, renders unchanged.

title: Remediate: encode_save writes saves larger than the 1 MiB cap that decode_save then refuses
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review]
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/app/saves.py, src/ravel/app/session.py, src/ravel/cli.py, docs/RAVEL_LANGUAGE_SPEC.md

**Finding**:
encode_save (saves.py:112) never checks its output against MAX_SAVE_BYTES, but _decode_save refuses anything over 1 MiB. A ~60 KB story (well inside every cap) with one 60,000-char string copied into 20 qualities encodes to 1,260,295 bytes; the save reports success ('Saved to X') and the later load fails with SaveCorruptError 'save file too large'. Silent loss of player progress; the declared 1 MiB cap is enforced on only one side of the round trip. Control characters make it worse (json escapes each as 6 bytes). Probed 2026-09-28.

**Fix suggestion**:
- Pre-check before json.dumps: estimate the encoded size (e.g. sum of string-quality lengths x worst-case escape factor, or encode and check len) and refuse over MAX_SAVE_BYTES, without first building a multi-GB string (a 1 MiB source can hold ~100K 'q_i = s' copies of a 60K string; state shares the str object but json.dumps does not).
- Raise a typed SessionError subclass (e.g. SaveTooLargeError); GameSession.save propagates it; ConsoleUI._save (catches only OSError today) reports it.
- Update docs/RAVEL_LANGUAGE_SPEC.md §E 'Save file size' row to say the cap applies on save too.

**Acceptance**:
- Test in tests/app/test_saves.py: a state whose canonical encoding exceeds MAX_SAVE_BYTES raises the typed error from encode_save; nothing is written (tests/app/test_session.py).
- Any bytes encode_save returns decode successfully (property/round-trip test).
- ConsoleUI test in tests/test_cli.py shows a readable 'Could not save' message, no traceback.
- 100% branch coverage, ruff, mypy clean.
close_reason: encode_save enforces 1 MiB cap via SaveTooLargeError; CLI reports it; specs updated

title: Remediate: save decode errors list unexpected keys unbounded in _check_keys
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review]
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/app/saves.py

**Finding**:
_check_keys (saves.py:163) builds its message with sorted(repr(key) for key in extra/missing) and no bound. A save with one 500,000-char extra top-level key gives a 500,024-char SaveCorruptError; 60,000 short extra keys give a 588,910-char message; the same happens in nested objects (state.stack[i].anchor). This bypasses the ravel-h6v.24 fix, which bounded other save-derived values but missed this path. repr() already escapes ESC, so the problem is length only.

**Fix suggestion**:
Use bounded_repr per key, and cap how many keys are listed (e.g. first 5 in sorted order, then 'and N more'). Apply to both missing and unexpected lists.

**Acceptance**:
- Tests in tests/app/test_saves.py: one huge extra key, and many extra keys (top level and nested anchor), each yield a SaveCorruptError whose message stays under a fixed bound (a few hundred chars) and still names the path label.
- 100% branch coverage, ruff, mypy clean.
close_reason: _check_keys bounds each key and caps listing at 5 + 'and N more'; wrapper errors bounded; tests added

title: Remediate: mid-line <> glue in a text line raises raw parsimonious IncompleteParseError
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review]
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/parsers.py

**Finding**:
PlainTextParser.parse (parsers.py:216) calls self.grammar['prose'].parse(prose) unguarded. The prose rule is text glue?, so any text line with <> anywhere except the end (e.g. 'a <> b', 'a<><>', '{x == 1} a <> b', 'text: a <> b') makes Environment.load() raise parsimonious IncompleteParseError, which is outside the ravel ParseError hierarchy. The raw message also quotes up to 20 chars of source unescaped, and cli.handle_exception logs it verbatim to the terminal. Spec (RAVEL_LANGUAGE_SPEC.md ~L496) defines <> only at end of text, so this is malformed input needing a typed error.

**Fix suggestion**:
Follow the ravel-h6v.23 IntroTextParser pattern: wrap the prose parse in try/except exceptions.ParsimoniousParseError and raise exceptions.ParseError('Invalid text line %s: %s' % (bounded_repr(text), printable(e))) from e. (Alternatively, decide mid-line <> is literal prose and change the grammar; either way no raw exception.)

**Acceptance**:
- Tests in tests/test_parsers.py for 'a <> b', 'a<><>', and '{x == 1} a <> b' raise ravel.exceptions.ParseError (not parsimonious errors), with a bounded, printable message.
- A MemoryStorySource load test shows the typed error reaches the public API.
- 100% branch coverage, ruff, mypy clean.
close_reason: Mid-line <> glue now raises typed ParseError with bounded excerpt; spec updated

title: Remediate: predicate sorting raises raw TypeError when one quality has mixed-type comparison values
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review]
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/compiler/rulesets.py, src/ravel/compiler/rulebooks.py, src/ravel/types.py

**Finding**:
compile_ruleset (rulesets.py:6) sorts Predicates, and compile_rulebook (rulebooks.py:137) heapq.merges them. attr.s gives Predicate/Comparison order=True, so two predicates on the same quality and comparator with differently typed right-hand sides compare e.g. 1 < 'a', 1 < QualityRef, Expression < int, Value < float, and Environment.load() raises a raw TypeError. Reproduced with 'when: [x > 1, x > y]', '[x > 1, x > "a"]', '[x > 1.5, x > value]', and a top-level 'when: x > 1' plus rule 'when: x > "a"' (fails in the lazy heapq.merge at list()). 'x > 1 and x > threshold' is a legitimate program, so it must compile.

**Fix suggestion**:
Do not catch and reject. Give predicates a total order: sort both sites with a key such as (p.name, p.predicate.comparator, repr(p.predicate)) and pass the same key to heapq.merge; or define ordering on the value types so mixed types never compare directly. Keep the common-predicates-first-on-ties behavior of the merge.

**Acceptance**:
- Tests in tests/test_compiler_rulesets.py and tests/test_compiler_rulebooks.py: the reproducing rulebooks above compile, and the story queries correctly (both predicates checked).
- The merged predicate order still equals sorting the concatenation with the same key (existing merge test still holds).
- 100% branch coverage, ruff, mypy clean.
close_reason: Total-order predicate sort key handles mixed-type operands

comments.author: eykd
comments.text: Orchestrator note: this crashes VALID stories (x > 1 alongside x > threshold is legitimate authoring), so it is a correctness bug, not just an untyped error. Fix the sort so mixed-type predicate values always order deterministically (e.g. key on (name, comparator, type-tag, repr)); ordering must stay stable and deterministic across runs (engine determinism guarantee, US4). Do NOT reject these stories. Add a Cloak-style acceptance-level test that such a story loads and plays.

title: Remediate: indentation nesting cap bypassed via Unicode line separators
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review]
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/environments.py

**Finding**:
_source_nesting_depth (environments.py:23) splits the source with str.splitlines(), which also breaks on \x0b \x0c \x1c \x1d \x1e \x85 \u2028 \u2029. syml breaks lines only on \n (after normalizing \r\n and \r). A separator placed inside each label (e.g. '- [c0]t\u2028z') shows up to the scanner as an indent-0 line that empties its stack, so the scanner reports depth 3 while syml builds ~380 real indentation levels. Verified: 190 nested choice: blocks load successfully although the declared cap (RAVEL_LANGUAGE_SPEC.md §E, 128 levels -> ParseError at load time) should refuse them. The 200 choice cap and the RecursionError catch still stop deeper input with typed errors, so this is a cap bypass, not a raw crash. It bypasses the ravel-h6v.14 fix.

**Fix suggestion**:
Split lines the way syml does: re.split(r'\r\n|\r|\n', source) (or normalize then split('\n')). Count indentation as leading spaces only (syml rejects tab indentation) and skip comments only at column 0 (# or //), matching syml's grammar. Optionally add a post-parse iterative depth check on the syml tree as a backstop.

**Acceptance**:
- A rulebook with \u2028 (and each of \x0b \x0c \x1c \x85) inside values and more than 128 real indentation levels raises the 128-cap ParseError
- Extend the existing ravel-h6v.14 nesting test with a parametrized separator case
- examples/cloak still loads; 100% branch coverage holds
close_reason: Nesting gate now lexes via syml preprocess/is_blank/grammar regexes; differential + 190-choice regression tests; filed ravel-h6v.33

title: Remediate: sibling choices whose labels slugify alike silently overwrite each other's bodies
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review]
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/compiler/directives.py

**Finding**:
compile_choice builds each choice's location as parent_rule::slugify(label), and _compile_directive_bodies / compile_choice merge the subsituation dicts with merge_dicts (last wins). Two sibling choices whose labels slugify to the same text ('[Go]' and '[go]', '[Go]' and '[Go!]', or two empty '[]' labels) get the same location. Verified: both Choice directives point at begin::s::go and only the second body ('B body') survives; the first choice's text and effects are silently dropped. No error is raised and the language spec does not document the rule. This is a valid story that loses data (in scope under the 2026-09-28 ruling). It is authored content, not player data, so it is filed at p3.

**Fix suggestion**:
In _compile_directive_bodies (and the top-level situation merge), detect a location key that appears in more than one subsituation dict before merging and raise ParseError naming the rule and the colliding label (bounded with printable/bounded_repr). Document in RAVEL_LANGUAGE_SPEC.md that sibling choice labels must be distinct after slugification.

**Acceptance**:
- A situation with choices '[Go]' and '[Go!]' raises ParseError naming the label
- Two empty '[]' sibling labels raise ParseError
- Identical labels in different parent situations still load
- examples/cloak still loads; 100% branch coverage holds

comments.author: eykd
comments.text: Orchestrator note: silently dropping authored story content is a correctness bug. Raise ParseError naming both labels and the shared slug (bounded excerpt helper). Check whether examples/cloak or any test story relies on colliding slugs before landing; if one does, report it rather than editing the story silently.

title: Remediate: parenthesis depth pre-check counts parens inside string literals and prose
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review]
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/parsers.py

**Finding**:
BaseExpressionParser._check_paren_depth (parsers.py:61) counts every '(' in the text, including those inside string literals, and PlainTextParser runs it over the whole 65,538-character window, which includes the prose after a {...} prefix. Valid stories are refused. Verified: 'effect: x = "((((((((((((((((((((( "' raises OperationParseError 'nests parentheses 21 deep'; a when: predicate with the same string raises ComparisonParseError; and a text line '{x == 0}' followed by prose with 21 '(' raises ComparisonParseError, while the same prose without the prefix loads. A valid story failing to load is in scope; typed error, so p3.

**Fix suggestion**:
Make the pre-check skip quoted string literals (the grammar's six quote forms: triple and single ", ', `) and bracketed quality names. For PlainTextParser, stop counting at the first '}' that closes the prefix (or at the end of the window when no prefix closes), so prose is never counted. Keep the check before grammar parsing so the RecursionError guard still holds for real nested parentheses.

**Acceptance**:
- An effect and a when: predicate whose string literal holds 21+ '(' compile
- A text line '{x == 0}' followed by prose with 21+ '(' compiles and keeps its predicate
- 21 real nested parentheses in an expression still raise the typed ParseError
- 100% branch coverage holds

comments.author: eykd
comments.text: Orchestrator note: _check_paren_depth must use the same tokenisation the grammar does (skip string literals in both quote styles; stop at the prefix's closing brace, reusing the ravel-h6v.21 grammar-window result rather than a second scan). Add a differential test: for random expressions under the cap, the gate never rejects what the grammar+depth-cap would accept.

title: Remediate: inline list-item chains (- - - x) nest past the 128 indentation cap without counting
description: Found while fixing ravel-h6v.30. syml's grammar nests list items within one line (value = structure / data, so '- - - x' is a list of lists). _source_nesting_depth in src/ravel/environments.py counts one level per line, so a single line of N '- ' markers reports depth 1 while syml builds N levels. At ~130 markers syml raises RecursionError, which compile_rulebook already converts to a typed ParseError ('nested too deeply'), so this is a declared-cap accuracy gap, not a crash. Fix: count each inline list marker (and an inline key after one) as a level at its own column, or document that the RecursionError catch is the backstop for intra-line nesting. Acceptance: a one-line chain of more than 128 list markers raises the 128-cap ParseError; Limits table in docs/RAVEL_LANGUAGE_SPEC.md stays accurate; 100% branch coverage holds.
close_reason: Nesting gate counts inline list markers and inline keys as levels; differential tests added

title: Remediate: long operator chains raise untyped RecursionError at evaluation time
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review]
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/parsers.py, src/ravel/types.py, src/ravel/engine/engine.py

**Finding**:
_fold_left (parsers.py:50) now parses arbitrarily long chains like `x = 1+1+...+1` (verified at 500/1500/5000 terms) into a left-deep Expression tree, and Expression.evaluate (types.py:113) recurses through it, raising a raw RecursionError at ~330+ terms. Comparison.__call__ only catches EvaluationError, so a deep `when:` predicate escapes the RT-13 'unevaluable -> False' contract and crashes query(); engine._apply_operation only catches EvaluationError, so a deep effect escapes the engine's typed-error surface mid-game. On master the same input failed at parse time; the branch moved the crash from compile to runtime, so an untrusted rulebook compiles cleanly and then crashes every start/choose.

**Fix suggestion**:
Add MAX_EXPRESSION_OPERANDS (e.g. 100, mirroring MAX_CHOICE_NESTING_DEPTH in compiler/directives.py) and have _fold_left raise a typed ParseError/OperationParseError when a chain exceeds it. Optionally also make Expression.evaluate iterative over left-deep trees.

**Acceptance**:
- Operation and comparison with more operands than the limit raise a typed ravel ParseError at compile time (MemoryStorySource.load()), never RecursionError
- A chain at the limit compiles and evaluates correctly
- Tests cover both effect and when: paths; 100% coverage holds
close_reason: Cap expression chain operands at 100 in _fold_left; typed ParseError at compile time

title: Remediate: nested parentheses in expressions raise untyped RecursionError at compile
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review]
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/grammars.py, src/ravel/parsers.py

**Finding**:
The primary rule (grammars.py:15) recurses through `(` expression `)`; ~200 nesting levels of parentheses in an effect or comparison make Parsimonious raise RecursionError, which propagates untyped out of Environment.load() / MemoryStorySource.load() (verified with 300 levels). The vector predates the branch but the rule was rewritten in this range.

**Fix suggestion**:
Wrap parse in OperationParser.parse (parsers.py:130) and give ComparisonParser/PlainTextParser the same wrapper: catch RecursionError and re-raise as a typed OperationParseError/ParseError naming the text. Better: pre-check parenthesis depth against a MAX_PAREN_DEPTH constant before calling Parsimonious.

**Acceptance**:
- Deeply nested parentheses in an effect, a when: predicate, and a {cond} text prefix raise a typed ravel ParseError from load(), never RecursionError
- Modest nesting still parses
- 100% coverage holds
close_reason: Cap paren nesting (20) and expression tree depth (200); typed ParseError; tests
